chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the most severely afflicted of the people are the Prophets عليهم السلام, then those who come after them, then the most exemplary and then the next most exemplary.

key_terms.الْأَمْثَلُ: the more exemplary, virtuous, or excellent
key_terms.يَلُونَهُمْ: follow them or come after them in rank

ai.seo_question: Who are the people most severely tested by affliction according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the greatest trials and afflictions are borne by the Prophets عليهم السلام, followed by those nearest to them in rank and virtue. It shows that severe tribulation is not a sign of distance from Allah, but often corresponds to spiritual excellence and moral station.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The most severely afflicted of the people are the Prophets<sup>as</sup>. Then those who follow them<sup>as</sup> (in status), then thereafter those similar to the previous group and so forth’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The trial (suffering hardships in life) of the prophets is the most difficult then is that for those next to the prophets in a (spiritual) position and thereafter those similar to the previous group and so forth.”
